chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from 'Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"A man does not perform li'an with the woman with whom he enjoys (consummates marriage)."
ai.seo_question: When does a husband perform li'an with his wife according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that the ritual of *li'an* (mutual imprecation) is inapplicable to a man and woman in *mut'ah* (temporary marriage) or permanent marriage after consummation, as the primary purpose of *li'an* is to resolve disputed paternity which is structurally distinct in these marital forms. Scholars note this highlights the jurisprudential nuance that *li'an* is specifically tied to the context of permanent marriage (*nikah al-mu'abbad*) where lineage attribution is the central concern, whereas *mut'ah* has different rules for offspring. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on the specific conditions under which paternity disputes can be legally resolved through oaths.
